properties.Landing Comments: Moderate to difficult. Surf likely. Paddle into river channel to avoid sand bars. Easier approach at high water.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping. No fees (2018). Best sites on top of dune S of river mouth. Sheltered.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. Attractive. Unique lagoon. Drift Whale Bay to N has area's finest white sand beach. See: Mquqwin Brooks Peninsula Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Jackobson Point northwest
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing all tides on moderate gradient gravel, sand beach in sheltered cove.  Accumulates drift logs after SE storms. E aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Upland cleared tent sites, Hammock opportunities. Shaded in afternoon. Well protected. Appears to have occasional use by commercial groups, fishers.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal stream at N end of beach. Anchorage, Provincial Boat Haven. Lagoon nearby. Short marked hiking trail across neck to Jackobson Point small sand beach in Ecological Reserve where camping not permitted. See: Mquqwin Brooks Peninsula Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Nasparti Pocket Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on pebble beach.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on beach.
properties.Other Comments: Small but adequate and quite secluded. See: Mquqwin Brooks Peninsula Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Rugged Point
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach to N of point protected from surf except in NE outflow wind. N aspect. Sand beaches S of point often have surf. Headlands give varying protection to parts. S aspect. Expect long carries.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach on N side of point has 2 -3 wooden tent platforms, cleared upland sites for additional tents, picnic table, picnic shelter, fire pit, composting toilet, metal food lockers. A beach 400 m to E beyond low rocks has 4-6 further tent sites, camp furniture, Random beach camping on sand at various locations depending on tides, plus on at least 3 separate S facing beaches across headland trail. Hammock opportunities. No fees (2025).
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creeks on S beach, E beach, W beach accessible on foot below hide tide or by headland trails. Awkward access to first creek on S beach, Year-round water at head of McLean Cove 0.8 NM NE by boat and at Sandpiper Creek 45 min along S beach.. Attractive. View. See: Rugged Point Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Resolution Park
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on low gradient gravel beach. N aspect. Gravel boat launch. Float, dock under repair 2020/21.
properties.Camp Comments: Developed maintained sites with fire pits, picnic tables. Toilets. No fees (2021).
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. View. Rough boat ramp usable at high tide. Floating dock. Located on gravel road to Fair Harbour about 10 km from Zeballos Halfway along, past prominent viewpoint, where road veers sharply right, is turnoff to Resolution Park (signed). AKA Rhodes Creek.

properties.Title: Spring Island south
properties.Landing Comments: Steep shell sand gravel beach. Recommend approaching from E. W side landing more exposed.  Surf in some conditions.
properties.Camp Comments: Sites in the trees N and S of tombolo plus numerous sites above beach but they can flood in storms. Wind may affect which sites can be reasonably used. Pit toilet in trees near rocks with old concrete pad. Recent observation 15 tenting areas.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive, popular site. Site excluded from Treaty Settlement Lands in 2008 Maa_nulth Treaty. Rest of Spring Island FN owned but subject to public access under same Treaty. Careful of Giant Hogweed. Can burn skin. Toilet requires repair. Paddlers need to be aware that in certain sea states (strong winds from SE or NW and swells), this site is not easy to reach from Kyuquot Sound or to leave in bad weather. Surrounded by reefs. Allow a weather day.

properties.Title: Vernaci Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected small shell, gravel, boulder beach. E aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Undeveloped. No fees. Camp in trees on benches above beach. 3-5 good sites available in clearing with tall trees surrounding. One potential site on other side of island. Hammock opportunities. Hazardous leaning tree reported 2022 over main site.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Quiet. Serves as overflow site for Charlies Beach. See: Bligh Island Marine Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Charlies Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on gravel, cobble beaches on both sides of isthmus. E side has finer gravel, more room for boat stowage. W side has some jagged bedrock. The fallen cedar and other leaning trees are easily seen when landing on the E side (preferred).
properties.Camp Comments: Dispersed camping permitted. No fees. 5 open sites in upland forest above W beach with kitchen area, food cache, composting toilet. Three smaller sites on E beach. Other upland sites on E side were compromised by a large cedar tree taking out other trees when it fell. Users should exercise caution and make their own assessments.
properties.Other Comments: Owner of float house in Cuttle Cove allowed some paddlers (June 2025) to obtain piped water. Other water sources very limited in summer. Anchorage. View. See: Bligh Island Marine Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Burdwood Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Sand beach. W aspect. W end of bay often has surf. NE corner, where the campsite is, may also have surf even in light winds. There is a small bay within the bay and to the southwest that is more protected from swell and has less surf. This bay is also suitable for beach camping above the high tide.
properties.Camp Comments: Undeveloped beach camping. One protected upland forest tent site at NE end of bay, with more sites on the sand, gravel nearby. Many options. The area of strongest surf is near the creek so suggested camping at the other end of the bay on the SW side of the beach. . The NE end of the bay has 2 sea caves with the one closest to camp having a back door entrance accessible in most tides.
properties.Other Comments: There is a tree leaning over the extended camping area at the NE end of the bay. The main area would not be affected, but campers should use caution as to where they set up their tent.

properties.Title: Escalante Point north
properties.Landing Comments: Exposed, reefs, subject to high surf. Broad sand beach. S end more protected. where kelp in cove between point, rocks reduces surf.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on attractive, exposed beach. Undeveloped. Space for many tents.
properties.Other Comments: Water at river 1 km N. View. Rugged hiking trail across point to Escalante Pt south. Park boundary at point - land to S is Hesquiat Peninsula Provincial Park. Huge Prov Rec Site 111 Ha. area runs N beyond Escalante River.

properties.Title: Heelboom Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on gravel beach.
properties.Camp Comments: About 6 well established upland sites, 3 more on beach. Space in cabin but reported dirty and has mice. At least 2 more possible beach sites. camping,
properties.Other Comments: Water source. Site needs toilet. Cabin might no longer be in usable condition. Anchorage, Provincial Boat Haven. Behind cabin, rough trail leads 4 hours to Great Cedar Loop, tree grove. Also accessible from Lemmens Inlet.

properties.Title: Rassier Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on smooth sand beach. Low gradient. S aspect. Protected from W, N.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on beach or on 2 small brushed upland sites in trees. Pit toilet (green throne) has recently filled, and has been moved to a fork down the trail. New hole was dug May 2025. Currently green throne is balanced on driftwood logs, centered over new pit. Functional and sturdy, but may not be a permanent solution. Old pit is overflowing with feces and is somewhat covered by sticks / grass. A new steel bear cache was dropped off last spring (2024), and was never installed. It is now semi buried on the beachFresh water should not be expected or depended upon anywhere on Vargas in summer months.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. 17.8 Ha Rec Site.

properties.Title: Pirates Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on moderate to steep gradient shell, gravel beach facing Ruxton Passage in cove S of Pirates Cove proper. Some exposure to S. Landing in Pirates Cove proper not advised.
properties.Camp Comments: Walk-in sites with wooden tent pads, picnic tables, 1 vault, 1 composting toilets. Access from beach top via stair up steep bank to N. No fires permitted. Campers must remove all garbage. Camping fees apply year-round. May pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2019) via Internet or in drop box near water pump. BC Parks Backcountry Registration
properties.Other Comments: Potable water at pump 200 m from tent area. Walking trails. 2 dinghy docks in main cove to NW. Anchorage in adjacent NW (main) cove. Search for: Pirates Cove Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Chivers Point
properties.Landing Comments: Sand, pebble, rock beach, rocky ridges at low water. Narrow approach. Beach mostly floods at high water. Exposed to NW. Bring boats up bank at highest water levels.
properties.Camp Comments: 8 wooden tent platforms. Vault toilet. Food cache. Picnic table at each tent site. 2 small overflow tent sites. Hammock opportunities. No fires permitted. Camping fees apply year-round. Pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites or pay at site. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2025) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View from point, low ridge above tent sites. Hiking trails. Most popular of 3 sites on island for paddlers. See: Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Cabin Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Boat run through rocks onto sand, pebbles or rock ledges between rock ribs at neck behind small promontory. Slight Exposure to N.  Alternative landing from SE at high water. Approach from NW suited to all tide levels unless blocked by drift logs.
properties.Camp Comments: Tent platforms for 2 tents, placed close together. Camp only on designated sites. 2 picnic tables. Pit toilet at Chivers Point site 10 min walk away. No fires permitted. Stairs lead up steep bank to main island trail. Camping fees apply year-round. Pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites or pay at site. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2025) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive, Bring water - closest available Montague Harbour Provincial Park, Dionisio Point Provincial Park. Promontory suited to day use. Hiking trails. See: Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Gooding Cove west
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach. Protected, especially from W and SW.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping at W end away from road access. Easier landing conditions for paddlers not accessing road.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek crossing beach near site. Possible launch site. Anchorage - Provincial Boat Haven.

properties.Title: Mahatta Creek
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing up river mouth near sign except for tides below 0.5 m. Alternate landing on beach to W is easy at all tides.
properties.Camp Comments: 5 or more sites on upland, connected by trail. Small boat storage areas beside trail near both beaches.
properties.Other Comments: Collect water at highest navigable point up creek at waterfall 0.7 NM. Attractive. Anchorage. Provincial Boat Haven near Koskimo Islands. Cache location: 50.459230°N; 127.867490°W

properties.Title: Rowley Reefs Peninsula north
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on very protected low gradient sand beach. No surf. N aspect. Bedrock, shingle at W side with steeper gradient.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach appears to flood at Springs. Some tent sites on upper beach. Upland sites at centre beach and in open forest near cabin may need minor brushing. User-maintained cabin in good condition 2015 but roof leak reported 2017. Pit toilet. Float near cabin.
properties.Other Comments: Seasonal creek near centre beach. Logging evident behind beach. Short hiking trail to Rowley Reefs Peninsula south starts at W end of beach.

properties.Title: Rowley Reefs Peninsula south
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on broad pebble, gravel beach with some sand. S aspect. Protected from NW. Possible surf in SW wind, swell but reefs, kelp protect shores close to NW entrance. Treat reefs to W carefully on approach.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping on fine gravel behind drift logs. Possible to clear upland level sites in mostly dense salal with open mossy forest behind. Good, large user-maintained public cabin. Stove. Propane cooker. Pit toilet. S aspect. Sunny.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at year-round creek approx 1 km S. Smaller seasonal creek closer to site. Hiking trails to Rowley Reefs Peninsula north from cabin and to Gooding Cove via old road, starting approx 750 m S along beach, marked by hung floats.

properties.Title: Kwakiutl Point
properties.Landing Comments: Use caution navigating between Kwakuitl Point and small reefs to protected beach. Easy landing on sand, gravel beach.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on beach. Random wilderness camping permitted. No fees (2018).
properties.Other Comments: Attractive interesting shoreline to explore in calm conditions. Less exposed to SW winds than other nearby sites. See Lawn Point Provincial Park

properties.Title: Chuish Island (Island 40)
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on partly protected sand, gravel beach of moderate gradient (3 to 5 %). NNE aspect. Optional S side landing at same E point.
properties.Camp Comments: 5 or more good, partly sheltered sites on gravel bench. Protected rustic kitchen area. Smaller sites among drift logs or on pebbly upper S beach and in grassy treed areas. No fees (2025). Green throne pit toilet on S side, W of main camp area, along short marked trail. Hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Aka Island 40 or Second Island. See: Nuchatlitz Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Catala Island south
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate sand, gravel, small cobble beaches exposed to surge, occasional surf, especially on pebble beach areas in W, NW winds. Gradient 3 to 5 percent. S, SW or SE aspects.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed. Several sheltered upland sites at point or in mossy forest. S aspect. Camp furniture. Fire pit. No fees (2025). Other exposed beach sites on coarse sand, pebble on either side of point. Hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Rock gardens, sea caves, tide pools, beach walks, wildlife viewing. See: Catala Island Provincial Marine Park.

properties.Title: Rosa Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on sheltered small beach of fine sand, moderate gradient. N aspect. Beach entrance not easily seen behind reef from some directions.
properties.Camp Comments: Several semi-developed upland tent sites of differing size. also some beach camping but little beach at Springs. Composting toilet. Metal food bins. Rustic kitchen area. Posted notice Re; no fires, no smoking. Reported Sept 2025: BC Parks has recommended not camping at Rosa due to unstable trees. They have done some work to remove hazards but not completed.You would want to use good judgment of overhead hazards if using the are in high winds.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Often busy - frequent drop-off point for water transport. Wildlife viewing. Sea otters. Anchorage - Provincial Boat Haven at rocky bay on E side of island. Short trail across island. See: Nuchatlitz Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Robert Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected sand beach.
properties.Camp Comments: 3 upland sites. Beach camping during moderate tides. Evidence of beach flooding during storms. One reporter describes as rough and somewhat inadequate campsite.
properties.Other Comments: Quiet, secluded. We have created a Vargas Island webpage with information about Ahousaht passes and a link to the Ahousaht map where there is allowable camping and day use.

properties.Title: Whitesand Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on broad sand beach. SE aspect. Occasional surf but more protected than Cow Bay.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach and upland camping.
properties.Other Comments: Wild Side hiking Trail to Cow Bay and Ahousaht village. $25 trail use fee (2014) applies outside park boundary. No camping fees (2018). Muddy hiking trail to warm spring in Matilda Inlet. Aka Gibson Marine Park, Whitesands Beach. See Wildside Trail See: Gibson Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Conover Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Difficult, awkward on rock shelves, in sheltered cove. Easier at high water on tiny beach of pebble, some sand. High public float difficult for paddlecraft unloading or launching. Mud at low water. Alternate landing in Honeymoon Bay on E side of island N48D 56.283M, W123D 32.650M
properties.Camp Comments: Numbered sites each with a picnic table plus possible additional random sites in open grass field, damp in Spring. Less suited for hammocks. Pit, vault toilets. No fires permitted. Food cache. Dining shelter. Camping fees apply year-round. May pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2025) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: Dock, busy anchorage. Historic buildings. Bring water - closest available at Montague Harbour Provincial Park or Dionisio Point Provincial Park. Hiking trails. Mostly used by boaters who moor at dock or in cove. See Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Montague Harbour sum'nuw
properties.Landing Comments: Easy shell, sand sheltered beaches on both sides of peninsula. Sand, mud at low water. Preferred beach E of dock near steps.
properties.Camp Comments: 28 designated walk-in sites of which 21 reservable mid-May to early-Sept. Fees apply year-round $25/night per party summer, $13 winter (2025). BC Parks Camping. Group shelter. Picnic tables. Food bins. Vault and pit toilets. Fires rings. Additional sites in damp but pleasant mowed field to NE of main site. 16 additional drive-in reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: Water at taps. Anchorage. Amphitheatre, dock, boat launch. Pub, restaurant nearby. Trails. See: Montague Harbour Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: James Bay Prevost Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected sand, gravel beach at high water. Low gradient. Mud, eel grass, long carry at low water. NW aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Sites in old orchard. Damp. Unmown tall grass may reduce sites usable for tenting. Also better sites in trees on adjacent high cove bank. Hammock opportunities. 4 picnic tables. Food cache. Composting toilet. Fee charged year-round $13.50 person/night (summer) $7.50 person/night (winter) 2025 rates. No fires, including below high tide mark. See camping
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal stream at bay head. Attractive. Popular anchorage. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. Walking trail to bay head continues to Peile Pt. Main beach at bay head might also known as O'Reilly Beach but unclear.

properties.Title: Sand Dune Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on broad sand beach. SE aspect. Occasional surf but more protected than Cow Bay.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach and upland camping with tent platform. Functioning composting toilet with step ladder angle with 5 steps to get up. (2024). Bear cache.
properties.Other Comments: Wild Side hiking Trail to Cow Bay and Ahousaht village. $25 trail use fee (2014) applies outside Park boundary. No camping fees (2018). See Wildside Trail. Aka Gibson Marine Park or Whitesands Beach. See: Gibson Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Maquinna Point
properties.Landing Comments: Avoid reefs on W side of beach as you approach - visible at mid tides. Surf less at mid beach or behind a reef except at high water.  Semi protected from NW, somewhat exposed to swell. Both Maquinna Point and Maquinna Point East are east of Maquinna Point and can be subject to swell, especially from the W and SW. Maquinna Point is easier to land here than at Maquinna Point East which has a steeper gradient beach. More protected at lower tide.  Mixture of sand, rounded cobbles.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on upper beach. Maquinna Point's beach has a low to medium gradient and it is a short headland walk away from Maquinna Lagoon and Maquinna beach that extends toward Yuquot.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. On Nootka hiking Trail. Short walk to Maquinna Pt. Outer Coast Nootka Island Recreation Site REC16199 as shown on IMAP.

properties.Title: Hunt Islets
properties.Landing Comments: N beach has preferred easy landing with boat run and small boat stowage area. S beach has boulders, rocks, unapproachable at mid, low tides.
properties.Camp Comments: 4 separate secluded campsites along trail connecting the N,S beaches. 3 more on S. beach upland. Green throne pit toilet.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive, comfortable site. Logbook cache located in stump at head of trail.

properties.Title: Quatsino Park Beaches
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on rock, pebble beaches.  Easiest on most easterly beach of group.  Steeper gradient on these beaches than elsewhere in the Sound so fewer low tide issues than elsewhere. S aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Possible to squeeze in one or two tents on each beach. Not enough room for 3 tents.
properties.Other Comments: Several small dispersed beaches suitable for one or two tents each. See Quatsino Provincial Park

properties.Title: Grant Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach. S aspect. Exposed to S, SW, wind, surf. Protected from NW winds, swell.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on grassy upland. Pit toilet.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creek. Trail access to road to Winter Harbour. Popular with hikers. W wind blows out of bay.

properties.Title: Escalante Point south
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on sand beach protected by reefs, Escalante Island. te?	The start of the 1 km trail to North Escalante Point is marked with buoys. However with some blowdowns and vegetation growth in the middle section of the trail, it would be wise to add more flagging tape to avoid following wolf or bear paths
properties.Camp Comments: 2022 ALERT: NO CAMPING AT REQUEST OF LOCAL FIRST NATIONS WITH SUPPORT OF BC PARKS.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. 1 km rugged hiking trail to Escalante Point north marked by buoys. Expect some blowdowns, Year-round water at Escalante R. See: Hesquiat Peninsula Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Balaklava Island Booms
properties.Landing Comments: Sheltered, landing on moderately steep smooth pebble, shale beach. Be aware of back eddy near shore. More difficult at high water.
properties.Camp Comments: Was at one time a very spacious, grassy site. Former log sort area now re-vegetating so needs serious brushing if more than a handful of tents are used. Rustic camp furniture.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at creek. Old roads for hiking. Former log dump. Strategic for paddling outside Nigei, Balaklava Islands.

properties.Title: Nahwitti River
properties.Landing Comments: Land at river mouth at W side of bay on sand beaches with N aspect. Subject to surf in high swell conditions, more so on E'erly shores.
properties.Camp Comments: Dispersed camping permitted. Camp on beach or in upland near river mouth. Pit toilet. Bear cache, toilet, tent pads at separate North Coast hiking trail. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: May paddle up river. Drinking water at river above tidal zone. On N Coast hiking Trail. Cabin ruins. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Harlequin Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on sand, crushed shell beach. Entrance to beach blocked at low water by rocks which might be fish trap weir.
properties.Camp Comments: Sites in 2 mossy forest clearings above steep bank on N side of bay. Picnic table. Random wilderness camping allowed. No fees. Obvious midden location, so fires should be particularly avoided except on beach. Potential for additional sites if brushed.
properties.Other Comments: Anchorage across bay. Trail across island from bay head to resort reported but not verified. See: God's Pocket Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Shell Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected shell beach at all water levels. S aspect. Vessel traffic hazards.
properties.Camp Comments: Gravel tent pads. Hammock opportunities. Pit toilet. Picnic tables, food cache bin. Sunny SW aspect. Fee charged year-round. First come, first served. No fires, including below high tide mark. Sensitive areas have been damaged by trampling, so avoid overflow camping. Large parties should use Princess Bay instead. See camping
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View. Extensive trails. Large midden. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.

properties.Title: Musgrave Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on sand, pebble, cobble beach. More rocks at small point. Protected from SE by islet. Sign visible from water. S aspect. Please do not land on sensitive small Musgrave Rock AKA 'Cactus Island' just off site.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach floods at Springs. Several sites on old road in upland at SE end of beach. 2 smaller, marginal beach-top sites on gravel. Picnic table. Pit toilet. No fires in upland. Vehicle accessible from Musgrave Road so roadway sites vulnerable to being driven over.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creek approx 300 m to SW. Attractive, view. From parking just off Musgrave Road, road leads SW to private residence, but branches S along old roadbed ending at site. Hiking trails in adjacent Musgrave Greenbelt including to 2 waterfalls. Rec Site area 35.5 Ha. Site maintained by Cowichan Kayak & Canoe Club.

properties.Title: Arbutus Point
properties.Landing Comments: Large moderate gradient shell beach W of point suited to most water levels. N aspect. Also choice of 2 closer easy shell beaches at high water only. Rock shelf at low water. Ship wash likely from frequent ferries.
properties.Camp Comments: Tent pads in trees. Composting toilet. Picnic tables. Fee charged year-round. First come, first served for campsites. No fires, including below high tide mark. Sensitive areas have been damaged by trampling, so avoid overflow camping. Hammock use restricted to trees with durable bark. Large parties should use Princess Bay instead. See camping
properties.Other Comments: View. Attractive. Wildlife viewing. Extensive walking trails. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. Fallen tree on trail to camping area, reported May 7, 2025.

properties.Title: Pool Point
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate on sand on SE with boulders to N. Approach from E or W sides.
properties.Camp Comments: Attractive. Open rocky area, trees.
properties.Other Comments: Views, close to former fishing resort in Double Bay. Small brackish rock pool. 2014 to be leased to commercial operator by Yukusam Heritage Society but currently unused by any known commercial operator.

properties.Title: Drake Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing in protected Pamphlet Cove with cleared boat runs through cobbles, boulders on two separate beaches. W aspect. BCMTN sign at the more northerly beach. Space at both beaches for boat stowage.
properties.Camp Comments: Main area near sign on level grass on foundation of former Central Hotel, store. Approx 10-12 sites. Secondary single large site for up to 3 tents under fir tree off beach to W but may flood at Springs. Green throne pit toilet.
properties.Other Comments: Historic settlement site. Boat wreck near secondary campsite. Short hiking trail between sites. Aka Limestone Island, Pamphlet Cove. Cache location: 50.520810°N; 127.655570°W

properties.Title: Yellow Bluff
properties.Landing Comments: Easy to moderate depending on swell height. Moderately steep gradient cobble, pebble, sand beach. Surf possible. Beach with E aspect NE of bluff most protected. Sheltered. Optional landing on sand, with W aspect across neck of bluff also offers shelter from NW.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping on sand in various locations on both sides of neck. No known upland tent sites. Hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Water at stream crossing beach across Yellow Bluff Bay to ENE 1.2 NM. It can be accessed using the trail from Yellow Bluff Bay across the isthmus to the bay (approximately 150 meters). Flow was steady, likely year round. Water had tannins. Might be possible to use old Port Eliza Main road to walk to stream. Alternative stream at Tatchu 13 Indian Reserve across bay to W. Other closer streams appear less reliable. Attractive. Staging for rounding Tatchu Point. Anchorage. Sea Cave Cove 1.6 NM to ENE might offer further sites. Area 108.9 Ha.

properties.Title: Haven Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on small low-gradient gravel, rock beach in well-protected cove.
properties.Camp Comments: In salal above beach with brushing. Some grassy areas might remain dry at Neaps. You can set up two tents on a grassy slope on creek left (approaching paddlers’ right of creek). Boats would need lifting onto rock ledge.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. Sometimes used as anchorage for very small boats. There are two fish farms across the inlet that can be herd until 11ish

properties.Title: Gregoire Point
properties.Landing Comments: Hazardous, exposed rock, reef barrier, boomers extend S from point. Kelp. Good protection from NW, W, SE inside barrier. When entering bay, watch for avoidable small surf wave that may form on left two thirds beside rocks.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites on sand. Comfortable, secure bad weather refuge.
properties.Other Comments: Reliable water source reported at stream N of point. Walk on beach, through bush 1 km from site or reach by boat. Attractive. Protected site on a difficult shoreline. Area 42.6 Ha.

properties.Title: Garden Point
properties.Landing Comments: Sand tombolo joins to islet. Approach from NE behind islet to sheltered sand, mud, shell, cobble beach. Low gradient beach dries far, so long carry at low water. At low water if swell low, approach from W to follow creek channel with steeper but unstable pebble bank onto moderate gradient pebble beach. N, NE aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Tent sites in shady or sheltered forested upland at base of tombolo, or on upper beach. Two brighter campsites on islet. Pit toilet unserviceable (2021). Fire pit. Hammock opportunities. Good all weather site.
properties.Other Comments: Water at year-round Brodick Creek alongside site. Attractive. View. Wildlife viewing. Some forestry work in progress behind site 2024, 2025.This site is located within the Nuchatlaht Nation's Aboriginal Title Lands. See map of the Title area here. Look up term of Aboriginal Title lands in our glossary.

properties.Title: Catala Island north
properties.Landing Comments: Easy to moderate landing on steep sand, gravel, cobble beach, depending on swell height, direction. Some shelter from SW. Expect surf on approaches in high wind conditions.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed among many drift logs. Camp near N point or on pebble bench. Limited camping off the beach. Several fire pits. E aspect. No shade. Unofficial pit toilet in need of maintenance 30 m inland from beach. No fees (2020)
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Sea caves nearby. MV Uchuck passes site. See: Catala Island Provincial Marine Park.

properties.Title: Shuttleworth Bight
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach. Light to moderate surf likely. Some protection from W. W side favoured, also has creek entering at extreme W.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach or upland camping. Large beach. Random wilderness camping allowed. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites. Hiking trail campsite located to W of Irony Creek mouth approx 1 NM to NE.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at creek. Historic settlement site. On N Coast hiking Trail. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Bell Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing in cove on protected white shell beach. Limited room for boat stowage.
properties.Camp Comments: Grassy, partially treed area on an obvious midden shelf above beach. Sheltered. Trail up to campsite can be very slippery and path closest to edge is giving way (so use inland path up and down if possible). No facilities. No fees. Avoid fires unless on beach.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Popular. Location gives access to multiple day trip options. Noisy generator at nearby fish farm reported to shut down 9 pm each evening. Overlooks fish farm. See: God's Pocket Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: Nolan Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on low gradient cobble beach. Long carry at low water.
properties.Camp Comments: Spacious, sheltered, grassy area between trees, towards point. Afternoon sun. Rustic camp furniture.
properties.Other Comments: Seasonal water at small creek. Attractive, popular site. Short trail. Glen-gla-ouch 5 Indian Reserve adjacent to W.

properties.Title: Nissen Bight
properties.Landing Comments: W beach is more protected.  Surf low to high.
properties.Camp Comments: Many sites among drift logs. W side floods at extreme tides. Pit toilet. Bear caches. Dispersed camping allowed. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: On Cape Scott and N Coast hiking Trails. Water at creek E of beach approx. 1 km from camp. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Songhees Creek
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on well protected steep cobble, gravel beach. 100 m carry at low water.
properties.Camp Comments: Spacious, semi-exposed camp on level gravel bar. Some protection from NW.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. Attractive. Road nearby.

properties.Title: San Josef  WFP Campground
properties.Landing Comments: Good dirt ramp to river.  Advisable to paddle river at high tide. Low water impedes 3 NM channel, gives high surf at river mouth.
properties.Camp Comments: NB. Road closure for bridge replacement Sept 2018. Developed campground. Picnic tables, pit toilets, fire pits. Nice secluded sites.
properties.Other Comments: Easy access to San Josef River. Overnight parking. May paddle river to access San Josef Bay. High water preferred. Western Forest Products San Josef Recreation site.

properties.Title: Union Island north
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on steep pebble beach at E side of small peninsula. Good protection.
properties.Camp Comments: Twin sites on both sides of peninsula neck usable at all water levels. E site preferred. Light use so some sites will need brushing. High step up bank to trail at W landing. 8 usable sites reported in 2022.
properties.Other Comments: Trail joins E to W beach. reported as overgrown 2022. Water at small seasonal stream at E end of E site. IMAP shows REC107035 Recreation Reserve.

properties.Title: Calvin Creek Falls
properties.Landing Comments: Exposed low gradient sand beach. SW aspect. Often difficult, expect high surf.
properties.Camp Comments: Most hikers are using sites next to the falls but the kayak sites on the north end of the beach showed very little evidence of prior use but take time to find. 4 upland sheltered sites. Additional sites on beach in good weather. Pit toilet.
properties.Other Comments: Water at falls. Campsite is used by hikers on Nootka (hiking) Trail.

properties.Title: Marvinas Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing. Broad protected beach of pebble and cobble.
properties.Camp Comments: Several possible sites. Old road bed behind beach offers flat areas but bush is mostly dense. S bank of large creek above beach is another option at most tides.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. Fishing resort and float home visible at N end of bay. Historic site.

properties.Title: Ahous Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Potentially difficult surf landing, light to heavy depending on conditions. N, S ends of overall large bay more protected, may be calm. S corner has hook for additional landing protection.
properties.Camp Comments: Entire expansive sand beach suited to camping. Random wilderness camping allowed. Composting toilet at Fingers at N end (rock bound coves). Please use animal-proof food bins at N and S ends of bay.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek in centre of bay. Attractive long sandy beach. Hiking trail across S Vargas I. See Vargas Island Provincial Park. See Vargas Island webpage with information on Ahousaht access passes.

properties.Title: Milties Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on gently sloped sand beach. N aspect. Sand bar to E.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp either end of beach or on upland clearing at E end. Centre of beach floods at moderate water levels. Entire beach floods at Springs. Please use animal-proof steel food bin. Green throne pit toilet in good condition (2019) but trail could use clearing as seen in 2024. Sometimes used by guided groups.There are two trails leading to open area upland tent sites and the beach is a pleasant area to walk. A safe refuge when the surf is too high and Dick and Janes Beach.
properties.Other Comments: Small seasonal creek enters W end. We have created a Vargas Island webpage with information about Ahousaht passes and a link to the Ahousaht map where there is allowable camping and day use.

properties.Title: Dick and Jane Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach. More protected than beaches on W of Vargas Island but subject to surf in some conditions.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed. Sheltered beach camping on sand among driftwood. Pit toilet. Please use animal-proof steel food bins. Note: See Vargas Island Provincial Park. See Vargas Island webpage with information on Ahousaht access passes. Two distinct sites at Dick and Jane beach. One at the top; northern corner of the beach and another midway along the beach. Both have food caches.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creek entering beach near S end. Some upland is private. Paddlers must respect owners privacy. Do not trespass. It's possible to pick up passes at Tofino Kayaking or Paddlewest Kayaking offices.

properties.Title: Narvaez Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Easy, on protected sand, gravel beach at all water levels. W aspect. Known as Little Bay.
properties.Camp Comments: Gravel tent pads. Picnic tables. Pit toilet. Food cache. Fee charged year-round. Reservable mid May - Sept. No fires, including below high tide mark. All sites reservable Overflow area for 3+ tents.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive bay, coves. Road access gated 1.3 km from beach area. Hiking trails to Monarch Head, Echo Bay. Swimming. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. See

properties.Title: Ruckle
properties.Landing Comments: Small exposed shell, pebble beach unsuited to high water levels 150 m SW of Beaver Point light, close to campsites on a mostly rocky shore. Alternative landings in sheltered coves to N or S, distant from camp area. Otherwise exposed rock shelves.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp at numbered sites in huge open field or under trees. Some tent platforms. Most sites non-reservable. Pit toilets. Picnic table at each tent site. Shared fire pits. 3 group sites. Wheelbarrows. Garbage collection. Field partly mowed twice each season.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive, View. Water at 6 taps. 7 km shoreline. Extensive trails, wildflowers. Intact historic farm. Trail access to road 200 - 600 m. Parking. See: Ruckle Park

properties.Title: Lawn Point
properties.Landing Comments: From N, take care when navigating around reefs. Usually better to approach in morning. Behind reefs, beach is well protected but expect surf in high S wind, swell. Reefs to SW.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites, on pebble, gravel, exposed to S. Random wilderness camping permitted. No fees (2020).
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Grassy peninsula deceivingly rugged. Historic plane crash monument. See Lawn Point Provincial Park

properties.Title: Keith River Site 4
properties.Landing Comments: Easy protected landing on sand beach in bay. This might be only at high water. A report received that at low to mid water levels landing difficult to see with large sections of beach fronted by rocks/reefs.
properties.Camp Comments: 3 or 4 beach sites, possibly fewer at Springs.
properties.Other Comments: Year-round water to N at Keith River. Attractive.

properties.Title: Newton Entrance
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on sand beach with moderate gradient except in strong SW conditions.  More protected than other nearby sites.  .
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping among drift logs. Protected from NW. Random wilderness camping permitted. No fees (2018).
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. See Lawn Point Provincial Park

properties.Title: Calvin Creek north
properties.Landing Comments: Landing moderate to difficult on low gradient sand beach. Prone to surf, especially near centre beach at Falls area, so N end usually preferred. Extensive low reef or shoal gives some protection at less than very high water levels. Swells break at outer edge rather than at beach so often minor at beach. Go wide of extensive shoals to W to clear offshore breaking waves.
properties.Camp Comments: Several sites on upper beach. Beach floods at higher tides or during storms. Report received that beach sites remain dry up to 3.9 m tide if tent is at forest edge, assuming no storm surge. Hiker shack, decorated with flotsam, in the woods. A new outhouse has been installed (one of those urine diversion toilets with the pedal).
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at falls. On Nootka (hiking) Trail.

properties.Title: Hanna Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing. Small, gently sloping cobble, pebble beach. SW aspect. Limited landing area at high water. Some exposure to SW wind.
properties.Camp Comments: Ample room behind beach logs. Small forest upland clearings could also support 2-3 tents. An overgrown roadway reported in area but not found during June 2025 assessment, however tenure sings present on beach.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creeks. Nearby fishing shacks, dock visible from parts of site.

properties.Title: Whaleview Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on sand, shell, gravel beach. Well protected from all directions.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed. Beach camping possible almost any tide including summer Springs. Small forested upland sites likely need brushing. Ahousaht Stewardship Fee required. Please avoid Ahousaht Nation Tootoowilteno Indian Reserve at E end of beach.
properties.Other Comments: Year-round water likely available by paddlecraft access to river approx. 0.5 NM to NE around point. Small, quiet, protected site. A good alternative to nearby Half Moon Beach in poor conditions. See:

properties.Title: Hesquiat Harbour
properties.Landing Comments: Long sweeping sand beach. Shallow, confused water. breaking waves over Hesquiat Bar.  Good protection beyond Bar. To avoid long carry at low water, avoid broad sand shelf at S corner of beach, adjacent to bar.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed. No fees (2018). Entire beach is suitable for camping. See: Hesquiat Peninsula Provincial Park.
properties.Other Comments: Water.

properties.Title: Obstruction Island
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate landing on sloping bedrock shoreline. Tricky at lowest tides.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping permitted. Rough camping on small level areas of rock, gravel, grass.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Anchorage - Provincial Boat Haven in cove.

properties.Title: Barcester Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient broad sand beach. Open to NW wind, swell. Expect low to high surf with less to S. Recommend use in settled conditions only.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping between drift logs. Some shelter from S.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at creek crossing beach at S end.

properties.Title: Isle de Lis
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on exposed gravel, pebble tombolo between Rum and Gooch Islands. Choose either N or S aspect depending on conditions.
properties.Camp Comments: 3 tent pads 150 m above beach. 2 pit toilets. Hammock opportunities. Fee charged year-round. No fires, including below high tide mark. Possible overflow site on tombolo. See camping
properties.Other Comments: On Rum Island. Small attractive island with views, trail. seal, bird colonies. Isle de Lis (Lily Island) name given by former owner. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.

properties.Title: Sidney Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy sheltered sand beach at all water levels. BW aspect. Small seasonal dock. W aspect. Lagoon closed to all boating.
properties.Camp Comments: Open grassy sites, tent pads. Picnic tables. Gear carts. Picnic shelter. Vault toilets. Fee charged year-round. Site closed for hunting 1 Nov - 28 Feb. Group camping site. No fires, including below high tide mark. IMPORTANT 100% reservable from May 15 to Sept 30 so paddlers advised to reserve. 2 small overflow areas. Mid-week sites often available on first come, first served basis. 250-654-4000,Toll-free: 1-866-944-1744. All sites reservable
properties.Other Comments: Site no longer offers drinking water. Trails. Swimming. Anchorage. Birding, fallow deer, wildlife. Frequent foot passenger ferry in summer from Sidney. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. See

properties.Title: Princess Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on beach in protected bay. Gravel at high water, mud at low water, some sand, pebble. SE aspect. Dinghy dock.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp in damp mown open field, an old orchard. Composting toilet. Picnic tables. Food cache. Short concrete steps give access up bank. Fees charged year-round. First come, first served. No fires, including below high tide mark. Suited to groups or overflow from smaller sites on Portland Island. See camping
properties.Other Comments: Anchorage. Small seasonal dock. Aka Tortoise Bay. Kanaka (Hawaiian) history. Volunteers provide information service in season. Extensive walking trails. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.

properties.Title: Paddlers Beach Raft Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Land to S of Macjack River mouth. Landing weather dependent but usually lower surf than on main beach. Protected from SW but expect high surf in strong NW winds.
properties.Camp Comments: Numerous sites on sand, gravel beach. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. May pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2018) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: Water at Macjack River upstream. Navigable for some distance. Hiking trail on N side of river leads in 2.5 km to industrial road. See:

properties.Title: DArcy Island
properties.Landing Comments: Pebble beach. Exposed to SE winds. Strong SE wind may cause hazardous steep surf conditions. Alternative beach, NNE aspect, nearby to N offers longer but easy carry to tent sites.
properties.Camp Comments: Gravel tent pads near beach with some shelter in mature forest. Pit toilet. 7 picnic tables. Hammock opportunities. Fee charged year-round. First come, first serve. No fires, including below high tide mark. See camping
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View. Rough trail across island to historic former leper colony. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.

properties.Title: Nordstrom Creek
properties.Landing Comments: Approx 100 m W of creek mouth, rocks of large outcrop extend into sea. Land at side of rocks in protected area about 6 m wide, navigating around reefs. Approach, landing depends on swell height, direction. Surf likely.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites on sand E of creek. Grass above beach too steep for tents. Random wilderness camping allowed. No fees (2018).
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. See: Mquqwin Brooks Peninsula Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Tongue Point west
properties.Landing Comments:
Moderate gradient all-tide sand beach protected from SW behind small rock islet. Approaches from both sides of islet well protected. W might be preferred. N aspect.
All tide landing to west of Rock protection with a small swell at times. Mid to high tide the landing to the east side of the rock fronting the Beach is more protected and provides and easy landing. Only at low low tides is the east side not as accessible.
properties.Camp Comments: Sand beach not really suitable for flat tent sites as sloped. Only one decent sized forested site with 2 very small nearby sites.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Aka Oldham Beach after Margaret and Ted Oldham, paddlers who spent many a summer week here. Recreation Reserve REC107007. Trail head to Louie Bay at easterly side of Beach. Trail marker to start but not well used trail.

properties.Title: Benson Point
properties.Landing Comments: Land E of point to avoid surf on W side. Easy on long sand, gravel beach. Gradient 3 - 5%. SE aspect. Moderate protection. Next beach to E is similar or better protected if overflow site needed.
properties.Camp Comments: Exposed beach sites. Aspect S , W. As of July 31, 2021 Warning: Benson Point currently has no toilet so BCMT strongly urges visitors to bring wag bags or similar to pack out human waste. On-site disposal is not recommended. There are a couple additional tent sites in the trees / sheltered from wind. Next beach to E suitable as overflow site.
properties.Other Comments: Small waterfall at far W end of beach had flow Aug 2022 so might be year-round. Similar report of creek with waterfall just above the beach, 0.6 NM W of site, but measured distance might be 1 NM instead. Attractive. Interesting shorelines. Sea caves. Lagoon nearby.

properties.Title: Third Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Extensive moderately steep sand beach at high water. Low gradient at low water. S aspect. Protected from NW. Prominent large treed rock outcrop at W entrance breaks swell for surf-free landing behind.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites on sand. Report of upland forest margin sites.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at year-round creek to E up along log into edge of woods. Freshwater bathing pool across E side of beach. Rope hang ladder on trail up onto treed rock outcrop. On Nootka (hiking) Trail. Frequently used as first night stop by hikers starting from Louie Bay. by float plane.

properties.Title: Strange Island
properties.Landing Comments:
Easy to moderately difficult at S end or elsewhere on long, 250+m gravel mixed rock, sand beach. Oysters at some water levels. Not enough beach space at high water to pull boat ashore. Middle beach area appears to be easiest for landing having a gentle slope and large sand/gravel areas at mid tides.
W beach required water exit, carrying boats up onto cobble/ boulder shore.
Slightly exposed to SW. Surf possible.
properties.Camp Comments: At least 6 tent sites behind driftwood logs for beach camping. However this option would be unsuitable during spring tides as the area may flood.Otherwise look for a blue line strung from hemlock to alder trees marking a trail into the forest (see photos). Follow the trail 40 meters inland to find 2-3 tent sites. The area could be opened up with some brushing work. Danger trees present in this area and therefore the inland tent sites would be unsafe in 40km+ winds.Aprox location of trailhead: 49.682887N, -126.599995W
properties.Other Comments: Attractive site. Work needed to remove danger trees from camping area.

properties.Title: Loquillilla Cove
properties.Landing Comments: 2 locations. Main beach: easy, on sand, gravel, cobble. SE aspect. E cove: easy, but some soft mud at low water. NW aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Sheltered sites in trees in both areas. 1 or 2 possible sites on main beach. Better camping in cove 0.5 NM E of main beach with spacious, level upland sites. Short walk to view over Goletas Channel.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creeks at SW, NE corners of main beach. Creek at SW hard to see but substantial. Creek on N side of E cove. Spring reported but location unknown.

properties.Title: Discovery Island
properties.Landing Comments: Pebble beach. Vessel wash. Strong currents near island. Pull kayaks up out of the water a bit higher as passing ships can cause larger hitting waves on the beach.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp only in designated large open field SW of Pandora Hill. Pit toilet. Picnic tables. Food caches. No fires or pets permitted. Camping fees apply year-round. Pre-pay via Internet, or use drop-box but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2019) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: See: Discovery Island.

properties.Title: Medallion Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Some exposure to surf. E side of beach usually preferred. W end of beach has low dunes causing erratic waves on lower tides.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping allowed. Camp on beach or on grassy upland. Many options. Composting toilet at W point of beach. Please use animal-proof steel food bin.
properties.Other Comments: See Vargas Island Provincial Park. See Vargas Island webpage with information on Ahousaht access passes. Link to the Ahousaht map showing where camping and day use allowed.

properties.Title: Cape Sutil
properties.Landing Comments: Easy to moderate landing on sand beach. E aspect. Protected from NW. N'erly of 2 beaches. Paddlers mostly land on S half of N beach.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites on sand. Dispersed camping permitted. N Coast hiking trail campsite around headland to SE has pit toilet, food cache, ranger yurt. Awkward access over logs in forest in first surge channel. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: Water at small seasonal creeks near N Coast hiking trail campsite. Attractive. Cape Sutil proper lies in I.R. so permission required to visit. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: San Josef Bay
properties.Landing Comments: 2 broad low-gradient sand beaches. Some surf. N beach provides more protection.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping. Pit toilets. Bear caches. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: Water at river or waterfall on stream crossing N beach. Popular site with hikers. Hiking trail 2.5 km to parking lot. Longer trails to Lowrie Bay, Cape Scott etc. Sea caves, stacks. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Cape Palmerston
properties.Landing Comments: Gravel, rock beach. Watch for some rocks, reefs.  Easier landing than Cape Palmerston Recreation Site just to N or some of the Raft Cove options just to S. Some protection from NW.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping. User maintained cabin.
properties.Other Comments: More protected in NW wind conditions than Raft Cove sites.

properties.Title: Topknot Point
properties.Landing Comments: Sand, gravel beach. Light to moderate surf landing at N end, E of prominent creek.
properties.Camp Comments: Exposed sites on sand, gravel above landing beach. Beach topography varies annually. Some more protected sites alongside smaller creek at centre beach.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at creeks. Visitor logbook at base of fir tree through salal underbrush at N50D 32.11M, W128D 12.681M.

properties.Title: Raft Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient sand beach. Easier landing S of river mouth. Expect surf at low water or when swell  exceeds 1 m.
properties.Camp Comments: Upland sites N of river mouth. Also beach camping. Spit at river mouth may be used as campsite. 5-6 toilets. 5 or 6 Food caches. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. May pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2018) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at river upstream. Macjack River navigable for some distance. Hiking trail 2.5 km to industrial road. See: Raft Cove Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Quatsino Park west
properties.Landing Comments: Easy launch, landing at low water on long cobble beach, S aspect,
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping depending on tide level. Little space. Too small for 4 tents.
properties.Other Comments: May be noisy due to proximity to Koskimo industrial area. See Quatsino Provincial Park AKA Prideaux Point.

properties.Title: Shelter Bay
properties.Land Tenure: Crown tenure - Section 17 designated use area
properties.Landing Comments: Easy, white sand, mud beach in protected cove accessible at all tides but high water preferred to allow site access from N side of sand tombolo. Kelp.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on sheltered white sand beach E of Wescott Pt at most tides or in approx. 6+ cleared sites in forested upland. Additional forest site at E end of beach.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek in NE corner is likely year-round. Located at N50D 57.89M, W127D 24.70M (WGS84). Intertidal life. Some commercial use. Some lands are 'designated use area'. Anchorage. Trail E of creek to First Nations site accessed by climbing a rope.

properties.Title: Cape Palmerston Recreation Site
properties.Landing Comments: Rocks, boulders at landing near river mouth. Gravel beach with high, unstable gravel berm above high water line.  Difficult to haul boats up.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on gravel beach. Likely 6 or more tent sites, but beach conditions change from year to year.
properties.Other Comments: RSTBC Recreation Site lies across river. Difficult haul with boats across creek. Toilet. Trail access to road.

properties.Title: Guise Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Difficult in SW wind. Surf, shallow sand beach.
properties.Camp Comments: Camping on beach, upland. Exposed to strong gap winds. Pit toilet on E side. Sheltered from NW but exposed otherwise. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead or pay site host, but no reservable sites. Frequent use by hikers.
properties.Other Comments: Water available seasonally. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Lowrie Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Broad sand beach. Expect surf. Difficult except in calm weather. SW portion by rocky outcrop usually easiest landing at high water, when poles at sand spit might be visible.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping. User maintained old cabin in good condition at last report 2014. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites. Green throne toilet. Report of overgrown trails (2021).
properties.Other Comments: Isolated. Attractive. Rough, muddy hiking trail to Sea Otter Cove, San Josef Bay. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Helen Islands
properties.Landing Comments: Sheltered, easy landing on pebble beach at mid to high water.  More difficult, large rocks, boulders, weed at lower water levels. W winds may bend to blow out of Sea Otter Cove. Landing on north beach is more sheltered and preferable.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on beach. Sites likely need leveling. Sheltered. Random wilderness camping permitted. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Lawn Point east
properties.Landing Comments: Pebble beach with easy to moderate landing depending on conditions. Surf possible.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping. More sheltered from wind, more secluded than main Lawn Point site. Random wilderness camping permitted. No fees (2018).
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. See Lawn Point Provincial Park

properties.Title: Heater Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on moderate gradient sand beach. NE aspect  Protected from W, SW. Landing on beaches on SW side of point subject to surf.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach sites on NE aspect beach. More space near point. Additional unlimited sites on other beaches but access more difficult due to surf.
properties.Other Comments: Possible water at creek, from small lake, crossing beach approx 200 m to E. Take rough trail across headland to beach on opposite side then head south across small 2nd headland to next beach, at the end of that beach is a very large cave work visiting.

properties.Title: Klaskino Anchorage
properties.Landing Comments: Protected from SE, SW. More protected in bad weather than Heater Point.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on gravel bench NE of creek. Roomy, protected site.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek. Provincial Boat Haven.

properties.Title: Red Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on steep exposed beach of cobble, pebble, sand, bedrock in cove N side Parson Bay. S aspect. At E end of beach. Dark slate outcrop nearby. Easier at mid to high water. Many rocks at low water.
properties.Camp Comments: Sheltered, attractive cleared tent sites. 3 tents on the lower level. A long and steep hike leads to many tent sites in the forest. Occasional commercial use reported.
properties.Other Comments: Views, wildlife viewing. Geological features, fossils. Good view of Blackney Passage. Vessel traffic.

properties.Title: Turnour Island
properties.Landing Comments: Bay N of rocky islet. Shell beach at mid water levels. Rock shelf, muck, clam bed at very low water. A few boulders. Land on either side of rocky peninsula. S side preferred.
properties.Camp Comments: Upland semi-developed level tent sites on duff in open second growth forest. Rustic furniture. Hammock opportunities. Additional level forest sites approx. 50 -100 m uphill.
properties.Other Comments: Large, well-established site.

properties.Title: Leg Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Sheltered sand, gravel, cobble beach in cove. NW aspect. Strong currents in Weynton Passage, Plumper Islands.
properties.Camp Comments: Semi-developed spacious site in forested upland. Rough kitchen.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Whale watching. Aka Mossy Knoll. One of the few sites on Hanson I that is sanctioned by Yukusam Heritage Society for public use.

properties.Title: Keith River
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing protected by rocks, reef, on low gradient sand beach.
properties.Camp Comments: 10-20 or more good all-tide beach sites.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. May walk on beach to Keith River Estuary on most tides.

properties.Title: Keith River Site 3
properties.Landing Comments: Easy landing on protected sand, gravel beach. Drift logs.
properties.Camp Comments: Drift logs hinder beach camping but sites can be found.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive.

properties.Title: Wy ash Island (Island 44)
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on sand, gravel beach. Sheltered on N, E sides. Gradient 3 to 5 percent. N aspect. Beaches on S shore, E point similar but more exposed to swell, wind.
properties.Camp Comments: Random camping allowed. No fees (2018). Most of tent sites on beach. Undeveloped sites on gravel bench at high water line on N side and in protected clearings in trees. 'Green Throne' toilets placed next to each other at NW corner of island. (July 2024: New Toilet Material has been delivered. 2 food cache bins. Some tent sites on S shore at undeveloped beach sites, also at SE point on gravel, pebble tombolo or in adjacent forest.
properties.Other Comments: 150 m hiking trail across to S beach. Gravel bar to Nuchatlitz Island IR to E dries on low tides. Sea otters. Aka Island 44. See: Nuchatlitz Provincial Park.This site is located within the Nuchatlaht Nation's Aboriginal Title Lands. See map of the Title area here. Look up term of Aboriginal Title lands in our glossary.

properties.Title: Belmont Point
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on broad sand, pebble beach. S aspect. Protected. Gradient 3-5%. Beach opposite near creek subject to surf.
properties.Camp Comments: Beach camping.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at creek at SE side of beach, via 500 m beach walk. Flowing July 2025, so might be year-round. Recreation Site REC6081.

properties.Title: Cow Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Exposed to surf, some submerged rocks. The SE and NW beaches offer more protection. Landing by the creek on south and slightly west end of Cow Bay is a protected area to land.
properties.Camp Comments: Random wilderness camping. Entire beach suitable for camping. Most popular places are SE end, NW beach or near information kiosk, tent pads, bear cache, pit toilets on SE beach.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Water at year-round stream crossing centre of W (Fourth) beach. Also seasonal creeks at other beaches e.g. near SE site. Avoid private residence at Fourth Beach - W'most beach, Camp instead on W side of stream or in another bay. Whale viewing. Wild Side hiking Trail to Ahousaht village has $25 trail use fee (2018) for area outside park. No camping fees (2018). See Wildside Trail for more info. See: Flores Island Provincial Park

properties.Title: Half Moon Beach Flores Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy to difficult landing on sand beach, depending on wind, swell. Exposed to SW. Rocks, boomers, some surf.
properties.Camp Comments: Lots of space on beach above high water.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Spectacular views. Do not confuse with Half Moon Bay near Tofino in Pacific Rim Park. See: Flores Island Provincial Park

properties.Title: Experiment Bight
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate on sand beach in wide bay. N aspect. Exposed with surf likely. W side normally preferred.
properties.Camp Comments: Exposed on sand. Pit toilet at Guise Bay. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead or pay site host, but no reservable sites.
properties.Other Comments: Less busy than other Cape Scott beaches. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Goodnuff Beach
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected pocket gravel beach at high water, large smooth rocks at low water. E aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Small sloped beach margin sites. Dense vegetation in upland. Reported space for 1 hammock. Marginal due to small size.
properties.Other Comments: Marginal site but suitable for emergency or transitory use.

properties.Title: Nels Bight
properties.Landing Comments: Some surf, long low gradient sand beach. Exposed but protected from S, NE
properties.Camp Comments: Beach or sheltered upland sites. Pit toilet. Food caches. Camping fees apply 1 May to 30 September. Either pre-pay permit via Internet or at San Josef Bay trailhead or pay site host, but no reservable sites. Ranger cabin (Park Facility Operator) at mid beach, reported to be open for public use Oct - May. Sleeps 6.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek or pipe. Most popular Cape Scott site with hikers. Can be very busy. See: Cape Scott Provincial Park

properties.Title: Newcastle Island Saysutshun
properties.Landing Comments: Generally easy, depending on water level. Land in channel between Newcastle, Protection Islands. Protected S or E aspect. Sand beach adjacent to boat shed. Mixed beaches of gravel, bedrock, sand, smaller rocks elsewhere. Oyster band at low water. Dinghy dock (fee charged), other options but hauling out boats officially restricted to developed S end of island. Vessel traffic.
properties.Camp Comments: Developed year round campground inland 300 m. from official landing beach. Picnic tables. Flush, vault toilets, hot showers. Dining shelters, food bins at some group sites. Pavilion. Food sold in summer. 5 large additional field sites for group camping nearer beach. Small boats may be wheeled or carried to campsites. Reservations available for half of sites. reservable mid-May to early-Sept. Fees apply year-round $18/night per party summer,$11 winter (2024). BC Parks
properties.Other Comments: Water at taps, extensive hiking trails, museum, history, wildlife. Frequent foot passenger ferry to Nanaimo. Anchorage, small vessel dock. See: Newcastle Island Marine Provincial Park. Snuneymuxw First Nation manage site.

properties.Title: Descanso Bay Regional Park
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected rock shelf at high water or small gravel beach at low water.
properties.Camp Comments: Developed year-round vehicle-accessible campground. Short walk from shore to camping area. Picnic tables, fire pits, flush, chemical toilets. Many sites have room for 2 tents. May reserve to be closer to water 250-247-8255. Resident attendant. Potable water.
properties.Other Comments: 595 Taylor Bay Road. Water at pumps. Kayak rentals avaiable. 1 km to ferry, village. Parking. Vehicle access by ferry from Nanaimo. 16 ha park run by Regional District of Nanaimo. Adjacent 50 ha Cox Community Park has hiking trails. See: Descanso Bay Regional Park.

properties.Title: Hardy Bay northwest
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on sheltered beach of small stones in protected cove. E aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Camp on pea gravel below drift logs, 1 large level site, 1 more smaller site. Site floods in tides above 4.6m. Subject to occasional drift log movement. No upland sites seen but if brushed has low slope so likely would yield hammock & tent sites.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Conveniently close to Pt Hardy.

properties.Title: Pig Ranch
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate gradient pebble beach in second bay from S. Beach floods at high water - logs awash. Boat run in mid beach section. W aspect. Exposed to NW wind.
properties.Camp Comments: Sheltered attractive tent sites in sloped forest. many more tent sites if brushed. Rustic kitchen area. Small trails between sites. Hammock opportunities. Composting toilet reported but not seen 2023.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creek but not seen 2023. Former commercial site - Views. See Qwiquallaaq/Boat Bay Conservancy.

properties.Title: Pig Ranch South Point
properties.Landing Comments: Moderately steep beach with many boulders at low water, smoother pebble, cobble, scattered boulders above. W aspect. Exposed to NW. Another rougher beach across neck of point offers access from S.
properties.Camp Comments: Semi exposed attractive sites in open at forest edge. Old platforms in disrepair (2023). Rustic kitchen area, table, benches. Additional sites if cleared of brush, debris. Currently not used commercially.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View. Trail nearby to Eagle Eye whale lookout, Boat Bay. See Qwiquallaaq/Boat Bay Conservancy. See 2013 management plan.

properties.Title: Sophia Islands west
properties.Landing Comments: Easy, rock/pebble/cobble only at mid water levels. Most or all beaches flood at high water making landing difficult on angular bedrock. Boulders present at low water. Exposed E aspect. Larger W island of group. Another high water landing beach reported on S side but unverified, unlikely viable at Springs.
properties.Camp Comments: Exposed, attractive small tent sites in open just above shoreline requiring difficult access up steep rocks. Challenging place to load, unload stow boats. At least 2 parties have tried to camp here but have given up.
properties.Other Comments: View, wild flowers. See Qwiquallaaq/Boat Bay Conservancy.

properties.Title: Francisco Island
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on protected pebble, cobble low gradient beach in either of two bays. S bay rougher, long carry at low water with some outcrops, boulders. Bay to NW has easier shore access but further from tent sites. SW aspect. Tidal rapids nearby. Landing on E shore subject to strong currents.
properties.Camp Comments: 3 sites brushed out at head of S bay. 2 sites brushed out at NW bay.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View. Staging for local channels. Rough trail leads to W bay

properties.Title: Surge Narrows north
properties.Landing Comments: Boat run through low gradient beach slightly to right of obvious grassy camp area viewed from water. Beach floods entirely. Strong currents nearby. Kelp. SE aspect, Beware of broken glass in beach silt.
properties.Camp Comments: Large open grass area between beach, forest. Sunny. Long grass can make summer tenting awkward.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal stream. View. Walking trail around point. See Surge Narrows Park.

properties.Title: Robertson Cove south
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on varied shingle, pebble, cobble beach. Exposed to W.
properties.Camp Comments: 1 clear upland sloping forest site. 2-3 sites on pebbles at either end of beach. Hammock opportunities. Pit toilet. Potential for many additional tent sites. User maintained wilderness site.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive, view. Old road. Hiking trail from centre beach 260 m to Robertson Lake on S side of creek which is often dry. Hike 10 min up trail for year-round water. See Ha'thayim (Von Donop) Marine Provincial Park

properties.Title: White Cliff Islets
properties.Landing Comments: Drying cove on SE of largest islet. Lifting boats from here is not easy. Alternative high water landing on exposed sloped rock shelf, slippery at low water. Feasible at low water when barnacles exposed. Visit only in settled weather, low swell, low wind. Little significant protection from wind, swell if conditions turn rough during or after landing. Waters to NE towards Owl I quickly turn rough when large ebb runs out of Knight Inlet.
properties.Camp Comments: Exposed, no shade. Grassy areas or level rock ledges offer some shelter from wind. Prone to overcrowding by large groups. Paddlers are known to have used NW islet as overflow site but not recommended. Essential to use sanitation method recommended in Code of Conduct.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. View. Wildlife viewing. See Broughton Archipelago Provincial Park.

properties.Title: Owl Island north
properties.Landing Comments: Pebble beach, small cobble, gravel in small cove at NW side of island. Mud at low water. N aspect. Boat run suited to tides to 0.1 m.
properties.Camp Comments: Open, spacious treed upland site. Mouldering toilet. Heavy use including by guided commercial groups. 2 rustic kitchen areas. Numerous hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Small trail leads across neck of land to boulder beach with W aspect for evening sun. See Broughton Archipelago Provincial Park

properties.Title: Diana Island east
properties.Land Tenure: Crown, Crown tenure - Section 17 designated use area
properties.Landing Comments: Pocket sand beach facing Helby Island. Low to moderate gradient. Protected NE aspect. Good for most water levels but little beach at high water. Floods at Springs. Some boulders at W end at high water.
properties.Camp Comments: Semi-cleared flat upland sites reported for 2 tents in the trees 10 m above beach. Potential for 4 more. Beach camping unreliable at Springs. Camp furniture. Basic toilet but not reported by most recent visitor. Hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Attractive. Easy access.

properties.Title: Turn Bay Recreation Site
properties.Landing Comments: Easy on low gradient sand, pebble, cobble beach in small bay. Beach mostly floods. W aspect but generally well protected.
properties.Camp Comments: Undeveloped. Camp on moderately level sites in open forest with easy shore access at creek mouth. Minor brushing, levelling likely needed. Numerous hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: Water at seasonal creek. Previously named East Thurlow Island west 1, Walkem Islands inside 1. Recreation Site (Reserve) named Turn Bay but it lies outside of Turn Bay proper. 8 Ha area.

properties.Title: Ramillies Channel ínaḵa Lhaxwm
properties.Landing Comments: Wide 7% gradient sand, gravel, pebble beach in small bay. Scattered boulders. NE aspect. Beach may flood at Springs. Drift logs. Prominent sign visible from water. Similar beaches to N.
properties.Camp Comments: Small level upland forest sites along narrow grassy bench just behind beach. Other possible small sites on pebble berm between drift logs except at Springs. Further options nearby. Composting toilet along shore trail heading to N up bank. All upland at the S end of the beach is private property. Please do not go beyond centre beach or posted signs. 2 aluminum food bins. Picnic table. Visitor log book. Fire bucket.
properties.Other Comments: View. Attractive. Year-round water available 1 NM N at Gambier Creek. Squamish (Coast Salish) name ínaḵa Lhaxwm. Please do not trespass on adjacent private property immediately to S. Site stewards: Sea Kayak Assn of BC.

properties.Title: Bold Island
properties.Landing Comments: Moderate on steep cobble, boulder beach. SW aspect. Drift logs. Easier access at high water. Protected except from S.
properties.Camp Comments: Undeveloped. Camp on old road that flattens above beach to W or on E side of beach. Minor brushing, levelling likely needed. Hammock opportunities.
properties.Other Comments: View. Secluded. Walking on old roads feasible. Beach fires are banned all year round.

properties.Title: Undercover Cove
properties.Landing Comments: Easy at all tides on steep beach of small cobbles. No large visible rocks at mid tide. SW aspect. Beach is not obvious at high water. BCMTN sign.
properties.Camp Comments: Short trail rises to level upland area. 4 cleared tent sites in sparse undergrowth, trees.
properties.Other Comments: Short hiking trail to lookout, further beach to E. Two small boat storage areas on upland above beach, beside sign or above beach centre. Cache location: 50.500366°N; 127.770371°W

properties.Title: Lewis Channel south
properties.Landing Comments: Unmaintained boat run on sharp rough boulder beach over coarse gravel. Low gradient at low water, but steep at high water. Some protection. W aspect.
properties.Camp Comments: Undeveloped. Fire pit. Flat area on headland for large tent, more sloping area for smaller tent. 1 or 2 mmall sites on coarse gravel at beach top, also1 small grassy spot reported by beach. Some overgrowth.
properties.Other Comments: Afternoon sun on bluff to N. Aka West Redonda.

properties.Title: Okisollo north entrance
properties.Landing Comments: Easy in sheltered, shallow bay. Mud, pebble, tidal grass. Bay dries at low water.
properties.Camp Comments: Sites in open forest or on narrow grassy bank. Damp grassy area near shore. Some reporters say it is gloomy.
properties.Other Comments: Water at creek.

properties.Title: Howcraft Bay
properties.Landing Comments: Low gradient mixed beach in large semi-protected bay. Long carry at low water. Patches of sand at all tide levels. Scattered boulders, bedrock outcrops. SW aspect.
